newsitem.title: UK: CE Energy scorns Northern Electric defence.
newsitem.headline: CE Energy scorns Northern Electric defence.

text.p: U.S. utility CE Energy on Tuesday rebuffed takeover target Northern Electric's defence bid to shareholders, saying it did not alter the fundamental value of the firm for which CE Energy was offering 650 pence per share.
UK's Northern Electric had said earlier it expected a 17 percent rise in its year dividend to 50 pence per share with growth over seven percent from then to the end of the century.

CE responded by saying: "Nothing in the board's latest announcements suggests that, in the absence of the final offers, ordinary shareholders would ever receive value close to the 650 pence in cash now being offered..."

CE Energy, 70 percent owned by CalEnergy, decided to raise its bid from 630 pence per share on Friday and set a deadline of December 20, just four days after UK Trade secretary Ian Lang is expected to decide whether the bid may proceed.
Northern chairman David Morris has said the company was worth more than 650 pence.
Northern on Friday had mentioned certain strategies which included plans to merge its electricity and gas supply businesses with those of another regional electricity company.
The UK firm also said it would develop a 50-megawatt gas-fired power station, in joint venture with Rolls Royce.
CE said the proposals lagged behind strategic initiatives already announced by other regional electricity companies.
